concept.body: SSS~ (SSS similarity): all THREE pairs of sides must share the SAME ratio. Steps: (1) order each triangle's sides; (2) divide corresponding pairs; (3) if all three ratios are equal, the triangles are similar and that ratio is the scale factor. One mismatched ratio means NOT similar.

explanationVariants: SSS~ requires all three side ratios to be equal.
Every one of the three pairs must share the same ratio.

widget.prompt: For SSS~ similarity, how many of the three side ratios must be equal?

commonErrors.feedback: 2 isn't enough — a third mismatched ratio breaks similarity. All 3 must match.
1 matching ratio says nothing. SSS~ needs all 3 side ratios equal.

steps.body: **SSS~** (SSS similarity): if all **three** pairs of sides are proportional — the same ratio for every pair — the triangles are similar. No angle needs checking; proportional sides alone force matching angles. It's congruence's SSS with 'equal' upgraded to 'in a constant ratio.'

widget.prompt: The preimage is the 3-4-5 triangle. Drag k until the image is the 9-12-15 triangle, and check all three sides as you go — not just the one you are watching.
widget.successFeedback: k = 3, and 3-4-5 has become 9-12-15 — every side tripled, which the perimeter readout reports as one number. That is SSS~: not three separate coincidences but a single dilation, so the triangles are similar and the scale factor is 3.
widget.lowFeedback: Not yet — the image is still short of 9-12-15. Keep raising k, and watch all three sides climb in step rather than one catching up to the others.
widget.highFeedback: Too far: the image has passed 9-12-15. Bring k down. No value of k stretches one side without stretching the other two by the same amount, which is the whole point.

predict.prompt: Triangle A is 3-4-5, triangle B is 9-12-15. Checking SSS~ means checking…

options.label: All three ratios, and finding they are equal
One ratio — the others must follow
The angles, since sides cannot settle similarity

predict.reveal: All three — the criterion is that they agree, and agreement is the thing being tested. What the dilation shows is why they agree when they do: one factor is acting on every side at once.

explanationVariants: ALL three ratios must match. If even one differs, the triangles aren't similar — proportionality must be uniform.
A single mismatched ratio breaks SSS~; every pair needs the same scale factor.

widget.prompt: Triangle A: 3, 4, 5. Triangle B: 6, 8, 9. Are they similar by SSS~?

options.label: No — 6/3 = 2 and 8/4 = 2, but 9/5 = 1.8, so the ratios differ
options.feedback: Two ratios are 2 but the third is 1.8 — not all equal, so NOT similar. Every ratio must match.

options.label: Yes — the sides are close enough
options.feedback: 'Close' isn't proportional. 9/5 = 1.8 ≠ 2, so SSS~ fails — the triangles are not similar.

options.label: Yes — two of the three ratios match
options.feedback: SSS~ needs ALL three to match. One mismatch (9/5 = 1.8) breaks similarity.

options.label: Cannot be determined
options.feedback: It can: compute all three ratios. Since 1.8 ≠ 2, they're not similar.

steps.body: To apply SSS~, pair sides **smallest-to-smallest, largest-to-largest** before taking ratios. Matching them out of order gives wrong ratios and false conclusions. Order the sides in each triangle, then divide corresponding pairs — all equal means similar.

widget.prompt: Triangle A has sides 5, 7, 10 and similar triangle B has smallest side 15. What is the scale factor from A to B?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 = 15 − 5 subtracts. Scale factor DIVIDES corresponding sides: 15 ÷ 5 = 3.
0.333 = 5 ÷ 15 inverts it. From A to B, divide B's side by A's: 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

explanationVariants: With scale factor 3, multiply each of A's sides: the side matching A's 7 is 7 × 3 = 21.
Every side of B is 3× the corresponding side of A: 7 × 3 = 21.

widget.prompt: Triangle A has sides 5, 7, 10; similar triangle B has scale factor 3. What is B's side corresponding to A's 7?

commonErrors.feedback: 10 = 7 + 3 adds. Multiply by the scale factor: 7 × 3 = 21.
2.33 = 7 ÷ 3 divides the wrong way. B is LARGER: 7 × 3 = 21.

steps.body: SSS~ vs congruent SSS, side by side: congruent SSS needs three EQUAL sides (ratio exactly 1); SSS~ needs three PROPORTIONAL sides (any constant ratio). Congruence is the special case where that ratio is 1. Same logic, one relaxed condition — and that's the pattern across all three similarity criteria.

widget.prompt: Two triangles have all three sides in the ratio 1 : 1. They are…

options.label: congruent (a special case of similar)
options.feedback: Ratio 1 means the sides are equal — congruent, which is similarity with scale factor 1.

options.label: similar but definitely not congruent
options.feedback: Ratio 1 makes the sides EQUAL, so they ARE congruent — the special case of similar at k = 1.

options.label: not similar
options.feedback: Equal ratios (even 1:1) mean similar; ratio 1 additionally makes them congruent.

options.label: impossible to have ratio 1
options.feedback: Ratio 1 is perfectly possible — it just means equal sides, i.e. congruent triangles.

hints: Compute all three ratios, pairing smallest-smallest and largest-largest.
Triangle A: 6, 9, 12. Triangle B: 8, 12, 16. Divide corresponding sides.
explanationVariants: 8/6 = 4/3, 12/9 = 4/3, 16/12 = 4/3 — all equal to 4/3, so similar by SSS~. The scale factor is 4/3.
Every ratio reduces to 4/3, confirming SSS~ similarity; the common scale factor is 4/3.

widget.prompt: Triangle A: 6, 9, 12. Triangle B: 8, 12, 16. Are they similar, and what is the scale factor?

options.label: Yes, similar with scale factor 4/3 (all ratios equal 4/3)
options.feedback: 8/6 = 12/9 = 16/12 = 4/3 — uniform ratio, so SSS~ similar with factor 4/3.

options.label: No, the sides aren't equal
options.feedback: SSS~ needs PROPORTIONAL, not equal, sides. All ratios are 4/3, so they ARE similar.

options.label: Yes, with scale factor 2
options.feedback: Scale factor 2 would need B = 12, 18, 24. Here the ratio is 8/6 = 4/3, not 2.

options.label: No, only two ratios match
options.feedback: All three match: 8/6 = 12/9 = 16/12 = 4/3. Similar by SSS~.

takeaways: SSS~: all three side pairs in the SAME ratio ⇒ similar (no angle needed).
Congruent SSS is the special case with ratio 1.
